observations.posthog_connection: Warehouse ingestion configuration now distinguishes between always-available and conditional tables, allowing PostHog warehouse connectors to avoid requesting unsupported resources unless the user explicitly opts in.

observations.behavior: Passes SHOULD_SYNC_DEFAULT into schema builder, changing behavior from unconditional inclusion to respecting opt-out status for certain endpoints.

observations.limitations: Only one connector (Commercetools) is shown. No tests, migration scripts, or release notes are provided. The change does not demonstrate broader systemic risk reduction across multiple components; it remains bounded to this single warehouse integration.

review.reason: Adds a new optional table with opt-in semantics and corresponding configuration and metadata. This is a substantive capability improvement: warehouse ingestion now supports conditional resource discovery rather than assuming all tables exist. However, the benefit is localized to this connector and lacks evidence of wider architectural impact or cross-component dependency handling.
review.posthog_relevance: Relevant to PostHog’s warehouse ingestion and warehouse-querying capabilities. Warehouse users could gain more complete product-variant coverage when using Commercetools as their warehouse, while avoiding unnecessary API calls or failures on Classic projects that do not expose variants separately.
review.uncertainty: The tier depends on whether other connectors will adopt similar opt-in patterns in future PRs, which cannot be established from this chunk alone.
